headline: Meta says medical researchers used its Muse AI models to produce ten health studies in four weeks, drawing on five million anonymised patient records.
score_reason: Concrete and large-scale, but a company self-report with no independent coverage yet.
importance_line: It could speed up how medical studies are written, which matters to researchers and later to patients, but the findings are observational and one outside reviewer called a sample study only hypothesis generating.
summary: Meta says in a post on its research site that medical researchers used a coding system powered by its Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse Wonder AI models, with access to a licensed database of five million anonymised health records, to produce ten research manuscripts in four weeks. Meta says peers, a biostatistician and outside experts reviewed each paper, but the reviews are published by Meta itself, and one reviewer called a sample study on heart-rhythm problems after endocarditis "hypothesis generating rather than practice changing".
notes: Company's own blog (39,000 characters read in part); expert reviews are quoted by Meta, not independent reporting. Muse models are Meta's own AI models.
